a034f061b2.d:
The Shukla-paksha Ekadashi of phālguna month is known as āmalakī-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
a034f061b2.s:
ಫಾಲ್ಗುನೇ ಮಾಸಿ ಶುಕ್ಲಾಯಾಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಂ ಜನಾರ್ದನಃ।  
ವಸತ್ಯಾಮಲಕೀವೃಕ್ಷೇ ಲಕ್ಷ್ಮ್ಯಾ ಸಹ ಜಗತ್ಪತಿಃ॥  
ತತ್ರ ಸಮ್ಪೂಜ್ಯ ದೇವೇಶಂ ಶಕ್ತ್ಯಾ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ ಪ್ರದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಮ್।  
ಉಪೋಷ್ಯ ವಿಧಿವತ್ ಕಲ್ಪಂ ವಿಷ್ಣುಲೋಕೇ ಮಹೀಯತೇ॥ (ನೃಸಿಂಹಪರಿಚರ್ಯಾ)  
  
ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಚ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮುಪೋಷಣಮ್।  
ಯದೀಚ್ಛೇದ್ವಿಷ್ಣುಸಾಯುಜ್ಯಂ ಶ್ರಿಯಂ ಸನ್ತತಿಮಾತ್ಮನಃ।  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಂ ನ ಭುಞ್ಜೀತ ಪಕ್ಷಯೋರುಭಯೋರಪಿ॥  
  
ಅದ್ಯ ಸ್ಥಿತ್ವಾ ನಿರಾಹಾರಃ ಶ್ವೋಭೂತೇ ಪರಮೇಶ್ವರ।  
ಭೋಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಪುಣ್ಡರೀಕಾಕ್ಷ ಶರಣಂ ಮೇ ಭವಾಚ್ಯುತ॥  
ಪ್ರಮಾದಾದಥವಾಽಽಲಸ್ಯಾದ್ಧರೇ ಕೇಶವ ಮಾಧವ।  
ವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಸ್ಯ ಚ ವೈ ವಿಘ್ನೋ ನ ಭವೇತ್ತ್ವತ್ಪ್ರಸಾದತಃ॥  
--ಪದ್ಮಪುರಾಣೇ  
  
ಶ್ರೀಬ್ರಹ್ಮವೈವರ್ತೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಖಣ್ಡೇ ಸೌತಿಶೌನಕಸಂವಾದೇ ನಾರದಂ ಪ್ರತಿ ಶಿವೋಪದೇಶೇ ಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾದಿವಿವರಣಂ ನಾಮ ಸಪ್ತವಿಂಶತಿತಮೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ---  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮನಾಹಾರಂ ಗೃಹೀ ವಿಪ್ರಶ್ಚ ಭಾರತೇ।  
ಸ ಚ ತಿಷ್ಠತಿ ವೈಕುಣ್ಠೇ ಯಾವದ್ವೈ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣೋ ವಯಃ॥೧೪॥  
  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಫಲಂ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಂ ಪಾದ್ಮಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಶಙ್ಖೋದ್ಧಾರೇ ನರಃ ಸ್ನಾತ್ವಾ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ದೇವಂ ಗದಾಧರಮ್॥೩೫॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಷು ಚತುರ್ಲಕ್ಷಂ ಯೋ ದದಾತಿ ನೃಪೋತ್ತಮ॥೩೬॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಪ್ರಭಾಸಕ್ಷೇತ್ರೇ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಗ್ರಹಣೇ ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯಯೋಃ॥೩೭॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಕೇದಾರೇ ಚೋದಕಂ ಪೀತ್ವಾ ಪುನರ್ಜನ್ಮ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ॥೩೮॥  
ತಥಾ ಚೈಕಾದಶೀ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಗರ್ಭವಾಸಕ್ಷಯಙ್ಕರೀ।  
ಅಶ್ವಮೇಧಸ್ಯ ಯಜ್ಞಸ್ಯ ಪೃಥಿವ್ಯಾಂ ಯತ್ಫಲಂ ಲಭೇತ್॥೩೯॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತಪಸ್ವಿನೋ ಗೃಹೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಭುಞ್ಜತೇ ಚ ದ್ವಿಜೋತ್ತಮಾಃ॥೪೦॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಗೋಸಹಸ್ರೇಣ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ದತ್ವಾ ವೇದಾನ್ತಪಾರಗೇ॥೪೧॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಯೇಷಾಂ ದೇಹೇ ತ್ರಯೋ ದೇವಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿಷ್ಣುಮಹೇಶ್ವರಾಃ॥೪೨॥  
ವಸನ್ತಿ ತೇಷಾಂ ತೇ ತುಲ್ಯಾ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತೇ ನರಾಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಕರ್ಮಾಣೋ ಯೇ ಭಕ್ತಾ ಹರಿಪೂಜಕಾಃ॥೪೩॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಪುಣ್ಯಸಙ್ಖ್ಯಾ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ।  
ಏತತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಭವೇತ್ ತಸ್ಯ ಯತ್ಸುರೈರಪಿ ದುರ್ಲಭಮ್॥೪೪॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀಸಮಂ ನಾಸ್ತಿ ವ್ರತಂ ಪಾಪಪ್ರಣಾಶನಮ್॥೧೧೮॥  
---ಶ್ರೀಪಾದ್ಮೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಪಞ್ಚಪಞ್ಚಾಶತ್ಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಮುತ್ತರಖಣ್ಡೇ ಉಮಾಮಹೇಶ್ವರಸಂವಾದೇ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುತ್ಪತ್ತಿ-ಮುರವಧೋ ನಾಮ ಚತ್ವಾರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ॥೪೦॥

a09e6f6896.s:
ಉದಯಾತ್ ಪ್ರಾಕ್ ಚತಸ್ರಸ್ತು ನಾಡಿಕಾ ಅರುಣೋದಯಃ।  
ತತ್ರ ಸ್ನಾನಂ ಪ್ರಶಂಸನ್ತಿ ಸ ಹಿ ಪುಣ್ಯತಮಃ ಸ್ಮೃತಃ॥  
ಬಲಂ ರೂಪಂ ಯಶೋ ಧರ್ಮಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಮಾಯುಃ ಸುಖಂ ಧೃತಿಮ್।  
ಆರೋಗ್ಯಂ ಪರಮಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ ಸ್ನಾನೇನ ಮಾನವಃ॥  
ಭವಿಷ್ಯೇ---  
ವೈಶಾಖೀ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೀ ಮಾಘೀ ಹ್ಯಾಷಾಢ್ಯಪ್ಯತಿಪುಣ್ಯದಾಃ।  
ಸ್ನಾನದಾನವಿಹೀನಾ ವೈ ತಾಸು ರೌರವಗಾಮಿನಃ॥  
ಕೃತ್ಯಸಾರಸಮುಚ್ಚಯೇ---  
ವೈಶಾಖಪೂರ್ಣಿಮಾಮಭಿಧಾಯ ವಿಷ್ಣುಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಕೃಷ್ಣಾಜಿನಂ ತಿಲಾನ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಾನ್ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಂ ಮಧುಸರ್ಪಿಷೀ।  
ದದಾತಿ ಯಸ್ತು ವಿಪ್ರಾಯ ಸರ್ವಂ ತರತಿ ದುಷ್ಕೃತಮ್॥ ಇತಿ।  
ಅಸ್ಯಾಂ ಗಙ್ಗಾಸ್ನಾನೇ ಓಂ ಅದ್ಯೇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಗಙ್ಗಾಸ್ನಾನಜನ್ಯಫಲಸಹಸ್ರಗುಣಾಧಿಕಫಲಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಿಕಾಮೋ ಗಙ್ಗಾಯಾಂ ಸ್ನಾನಮಹಂ ಕರಿಷ್ಯೇ।  
ಸ್ಮೃತಿ-ಕೌಸ್ತುಭೇ---  
ನಿರ್ಣಯಾಮೃತೇ ಯಮಗಾಥಾಸು---  
ಯಸ್ತು ಕೃಷ್ಣಾಜಿನಂ ದದ್ಯಾತ್ಸಖುರಂ ಶೃಙ್ಗಸಂಯುತಮ್।  
ತಿಲೈಃ ಪ್ರಚ್ಛಾದ್ಯ ವಾಸೋಭಿಃ ಸರ್ವರತ್ನೈರಲಙ್ಕೃತಮ್॥  
ವೈಶಾಖ್ಯಾಂ ಪೌರ್ಣಮಾಸ್ಯಾಂ ತು ವಿಶಾಖಾಸು ವಿಶೇಷತಃ।  
ಸಸಮುದ್ರಗುಹಾ ತೇನ ಸಶೈಲವನಕಾನನಾ।  
ಸಪ್ತದ್ವೀಪಾನ್ವಿತಾ ದತ್ತಾ ಪೃಥಿವೀ ನಾತ್ರ ಸಂಶಯಃ॥

a0b941d79d.d:

a0b941d79d.s:
ಮೇಷೇ ಚ ಗಙ್ಗಾ ವೃಷಭೇ ಚ ನರ್ಮದಾ ಯುಗ್ಮೇ ಚ ವಾಣೀ ಯಮುನಾ ಕುಲೀರೇ  
ಗೋದಾವರೀ ಸಿಂಹಗತೇ ಚ ಕನ್ಯಾಙ್ಗತೇ ದೇವಗುರೌ ಚ ಕೃಷ್ಣಾ।  
ಕಾವೇರೀ ತೌಲ್ಯಾಂ ಅಲಿತಾಮ್ರಪರ್ಣೀ ಚಾಪೇ ಚ ಸಿನ್ಧು ಮಕರೇ ಚ ಭದ್ರಾ  
ಘಟೇ ಗುರೌ ಭೀಮರಥೀ ಪ್ರಣೀತಾ ಮೀನೇ ಗತೇ ಪುಷ್ಕರಮಾಹುರಾರ್ಯಾಃ॥  
ಯದಾ ರಾಶಿ-ಪ್ರವೇಶಃ ಸ್ಯಾತ್ತದಾ ಪ್ರಭೃತಿ ಸರ್ವದಾ।  
ದ್ವಾದಶಾಹಮಿತೇ ಕಾಲೇ ವಸ್ತವ್ಯಂ ತು ಮಮಾಽಽಜ್ಞಯಾ॥  
ಆವತ್ಸರಂ ತು ವಸ್ತವ್ಯಂ ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನೇ ದ್ವಿಮುಹೂರ್ತಕಮ್।  
ಅನ್ತೇ ದ್ವಾದಶ ವಸ್ತವ್ಯಂ ದಿನಾನಿ ಚ ಯಥಾಸುಖಮ್॥

a1311e133b.d:
When the transit of the Sun (saṅkrānti) happens in the first half of the day (pūrvāhṇa) or after midnight of the previous day, the first half of the day form a puṇyakāla for various observances. In addition to 16 ghatikas on either side of the transition, and specific puṇyakālas like ṣaḍaśīti, viṣṇupadī etc., this is also useful, especially in cases where the other puṇyakālas are inconvenient for appropriate performance of rituals such as snāna, dāna, tarpaṇa, etc.

While the nirayana puṇyakāla-s are well known, marked by the transit of the Sun into various rāśī-s (which confer the name to the corresponding saura month), there are also ayana-s and sāyana saṅkramaṇa-s, which mark the position of the Sun above the Northern or Southern parts of the Earth. These determine the r̥tu-s, and also the very famous uttarāyaṇa and dakṣināyana (movement of the Sun towards North or South, respectively). While these two types of puṇyakāla-s (sāyana and nirayana) coincided millennia ago, there has been a gradual precession of the equinoxes, owing to the nature of the Earth's rotation, causing the sāyana saṅkramaṇa-s to happen about 24 days before the nirayana saṅkramaṇa-s. In that era, uttarāyaṇa coincided with makara-saṅkramaṇa and dakṣināyana coincided with karkaṭaka-saṅkramaṇa, and the mēsa and tulā saṅkramaṇa-s corresponded to the equinoxes, when the Sun rises direct East (and sets direct West).

Many Dharma Shastra texts recognise the separate puṇyakāla-s for both types of saṅkramaṇa-s. The vachanam of Jaabaali Maharshi is mentioned above, where he says that the puṇyakāla-s are identical (in their reckoning) for both types of saṅkramaṇa-s. In the Pulastya Siddhanta, the anushthanas which are to be performed in this sayana punya kala just like nirayana are explicitly stated: snāna, dāna, japa, śrāddha, vrata, hōma, etc. In Kala Madhava, which is considered as the source text of the kala vicharas of the Dikshitiya, it is said in the 5th prakarana that,  meṣādi-saṅkrāntayo yasmin dine bhavanti tasmād dināt pūrvebhyaḥ ekādaśabhyo dinebhyaḥ prācīne dine, noting that Sayana Sankramanas occurred ~11 days before the day when the Mesha Sankramanas etc occur. Further references are seen in Dharma Sindhu first pariccheda, Jayasimha Kalpadruma sankranti nirnaya and Nirnaya Sindhu first pariccheda. There are also ample references in Vedas, illustrating how Ayana-s happened much later (in certain other eras), e.g. Shukla Yajur Veda Shatapatha Brahmana (Ekapaat Kanda 1/2/3), Nakshatra Sukta belonging to the Atharva Veda (Shaunaka Samhita 19/7/2), Maitrayaniya Aranyaka (6/14), and Taittiriya Brahmana (1/5/2).

For a wonderfully detailed exposition on the topic, see https://sites.google.com/view/nakshatradarsha/dakshinayana-en and https://sites.google.com/view/nakshatradarsha/uttarayana-en .
a1311e133b.s:
ಜಾಬಾಲಿಃ---  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಷು ಯಥಾ ಕಾಲಸ್ತದೀಯೇಽಪ್ಯಯನೇ ತಥಾ।  
ಪುಲಸ್ತ್ಯ-ಸಿದ್ಧಾನ್ತೇ---  
ಅಯನಾಂಶ-ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತೋ ಭಾನುಃ ನಾಲೇ ಚರತಿ ಸರ್ವದಾ।  
ಅಮುಖ್ಯಾ ರಾಶಿಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಃ ತುಲ್ಯಃ ಕಾಲವಿಧಿಸ್ತಯೋಃ।  
ಸ್ನಾನ-ದಾನ-ಜಪ-ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧ-ವ್ರತ-ಹೋಮಾದಿ-ಕರ್ಮಭಿಃ।

ಪೌಷಕೃತ್ಯಂ ಮಹಾಭಾರತೇ---

ವಾಮನಪುರಾಣೇ---

a215621189.b: Observed on Ārdrā nakshatra of Makaraḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
a215621189.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

In Kannamangalam, a part of the Chola kingdom, there was a wealthy Vellala named Thayanar who exemplified the ideal householder life, as praised by the Nayanmar Tiruvalluvar. Thayanar was a devoted follower of Bhagavan Shiva, expressing his devotion through a daily ritual of offering food made of red rice, a red herb sauce, and mango pickle to the deity. This humble offering was a symbol of his deep faith.

However, Thayanar's faith was to be tested by Bhagavan Shiva. Suddenly, he found himself in poverty, and despite this, he continued his ritual by working and earning red rice as wages. He maintained his devotion by consuming inferior khar rice, reserving the red rice solely for the deity. Further testing Thayanar's devotion, all fields in the area began to produce only red rice, but Thayanar refrained from consuming it, instead eating green leaves from his garden. When even these leaves withered away, Thayanar subsisted on water alone, his focus unwavering from his worship.

One day, while weak and emaciated, Thayanar fell while carrying his offering to Bhagavan Shiva, spilling it on the ground. Distraught, he believed he had committed a grave sin and begged for Bhagavan's forgiveness, threatening to end his own life with a sickle if Bhagavan did not accept his spilled offering. This extreme act of devotion touched Bhagavan Shiva, who intervened just as Thayanar was about to harm himself. Thayanar heard the sound of the deity eating the mango pickle, realizing the divine play at hand. Bhagavan Shiva and Mother Parvati then appeared before him, commending his extraordinary devotion and promising him and his wife a place in the divine abode.
a215621189.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

a303e5d14e.d: One must not bathe in many (small) rivers during the rainy season. Especially for the first three days of Karkataka masa, these rivers are impure. However, this does not apply to the Mahanadis, owing to their greatness, including Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Godavari, Kaveri, Shona, Penna, and the Pancha Gangas (Kaveri, Tungabhadra, Krishnaveni, Gautami, Bhagirathi). Exceptions are made in the case of Upakarma, Utsarga, Grahanam, Preta snanam etc., and when new water can be mixed in these rivers, and when there is a lack of other water sources.
a303e5d14e.s:
ಅತ್ರಿಃ---  
ಸಿಂಹಕರ್ಕಟಯೋರ್ಮಧ್ಯೇ ಸರ್ವಾ ನದ್ಯೋ ರಜಸ್ವಲಾಃ।  
ನ ಸ್ನಾನಾದೀನಿ ಕರ್ಮಾಣಿ ತಾಸು ಕುರ್ವೀತ ಮಾನವಃ॥  
ಯೋಗಯಾಜ್ಞವಲ್ಕ್ಯಃ---  
ರಜೋದುಷ್ಟೇಽಮ್ಭಸಿ ಸ್ನಾನಂ ವರ್ಜ್ಯಂ ನದ್ಯಾದಿಷು ದ್ವಿಜೈಃ।  
ಕದರ್ಥಿತಂ ರಜಸ್ತೇಷಾಂ ಸನ್ಧ್ಯೋಪಾಸ್ತಿಶ್ಚ ತರ್ಪಣಮ್  
ವ್ಯಾಘ್ರಪಾದಃ---  
ಸಿಂಹಕರ್ಕಟಯೋರ್ಮಧ್ಯೇ ಸರ್ವಾ ನದ್ಯೋ ರಜಸ್ವಲಾಃ।  
ತಾಸು ಸ್ನಾನಂ ನ ಕುರ್ವೀತ ವರ್ಜಯಿತ್ವಾ ಸಮುದ್ರಗಾಃ॥  
ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ---  
ಕರ್ಕಟಾದೌ ರಜೋದುಷ್ಟಾ ಗೋಮತೀ ವಾಸರತ್ರಯಮ್।  
ಚನ್ದ್ರಭಾಗಾ ಸತೀ ಸಿನ್ಧುಃ ಸರಯೂನರ್ಮದಾ ತಥಾ॥  
ಅತ್ರಾಪವಾದಮಾಹ ಮರೀಚಿಃ---  
ಆದಿತ್ಯದುಹಿತಾ ಗಙ್ಗಾ ಪ್ಲಕ್ಷಜಾತಾ ಸರಸ್ವತೀ।  
ರಜಸಾ ನಾಭಿಭೂಯನ್ತೇ ಯೇ ಚಾನ್ಯೇ ನದಸಂಜ್ಞಿತಾಃ॥  
ಮಾರ್ಕಣ್ಡೇಯಃ---  
ಕಾಲಿನ್ದೀ ಗೌತಮೀ ಗಙ್ಗಾ ವೇಣಿಕಾ ಚ ಸರಸ್ವತೀ।  
ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಾದಾಭಿಜಾತ್ಯಾಚ ರಜೋ ನಾಭಿಭವತ್ಯಮೂಃ॥  
ಜಾಹ್ನವ್ಯಾದಿತ್ಯಸಮ್ಭೂತಾ ಪ್ಲಕ್ಷಜಾತಾ ಸರಸ್ವತೀ।  
ರಜಸಾ ನೈವ ದುಷ್ಯನ್ತಿ ನದಾಃ ಕೃಷ್ಣಾ ಚ ವೇಣಿಕಾ॥  
ವಾಮನಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಸರಸ್ವತೀ ನದೀ ಪುಣ್ಯಾ ತಥಾ ವೈತರಣೀ ನದೀ।  
ಆಪಗಾ ಚ ಮಹಾಪುಣ್ಯಾ ಗಙ್ಗಾ ಮನ್ದಾಕಿನೀ ತಥಾ॥  
ಮಧುಪ್ರವಾಹಾಂಽಶುಮತೀ ಕೌಶಿಕೀ ಪಾಪನಾಶಿನೀ।  
ದೃಷದ್ವತೀ ಮಹಾಪುಣ್ಯಾ ತಥಾ ವೈತರಣೀ ನದೀ॥  
ಏತಾಸಾಮುದಕಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ವರ್ಷಾಕಾಲೇ ಪ್ರವರ್ದ್ಧಿತಮ್।  
ರಜಸ್ವಲಾತ್ವಮೇತಾಸಾಂ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ ನ ಕದಾಚನ॥  
ಯಮಃ---  
ಗಙ್ಗಾ ಧರ್ಮೋದ್ಭವಾ ಪುಣ್ಯಾ ಯಮುನಾ ಚ ಸರಸ್ವತೀ।  
ಅನ್ತರ್ಗತರಜೋಯೋಗಾಃ ಸರ್ವಾಹಃಸ್ವಪಿ ಚಾಮಲಾಃ॥  
ಕಾಲಾದರ್ಶಃ---  
ಸಿಂಹಕರ್ಕಟಯೋರ್ನದ್ಯಃ ಸರ್ವಾ ಏವ ರಜಸ್ವಲಾಃ।  
ತ್ರಿದಿನಂ ಸ್ಯುರ್ಮಹಾನದ್ಯೋ ಗೋದಾಂ ಪೇಣ್ಣಾಂ ಸರಸ್ವತೀಮ್।  
ಭಾಗೀರಥೀಂ ಚ ಕಾಲಿನ್ದೀ ನದಾನ್ ಶೋಣಾದಿಕಾನ್ ವಿನಾ॥  
ಕೇಚಿತ್ತು–--  
ಯಾ ನಿಸ್ಸೃತಾ ನದಾಃ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಾ ಯಾಶ್ಚ ಗಙ್ಗೇತಿ ಕೀರ್ತಿತಾಃ।  
ಏತಾಸಾಂ ಕರ್ಕಟೇ ಭಾನೌ ರಜೋದೋಷೋ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ॥  
ಕಾವೇರೀತುಙ್ಗಭದ್ರಾ ಚ ಕೃಷ್ಣವೇಣೀ ಚ ಗೌತಮೀ।  
ಭಾಗೀರಥೀ ಚ ವಿಖ್ಯಾತಾ ಪಞ್ಚಗಙ್ಗಾಃ ಪ್ರಕೀರ್ತಿತಾಃ॥  
ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ---  
ಉಪಾಕರ್ಮಣಿ ಚೋತ್ಸರ್ಗೇ ಪ್ರೇತಸ್ನಾನೇ ತಥೈವ ಚ।  
ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯಗ್ರಹೇ ಚೈವ ರಜೋದೋಷೋ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ॥  
ಮಹದಮ್ಬುಸಮಂ ವಾಽಪಿ ಯದಿ ತಿಷ್ಠೇತ್ ಪುರಾತನಮ್।  
ನವಾಮ್ಬು ಮಿಶ್ರಿತಂ ತೇನ ನ ದುಷ್ಟಮಿತಿ ಸೂರಯಃ॥   
ವ್ಯಾಘ್ರಪಾದಃ---  
ಅಭಾವೇ ಕೂಪವಾಪೀನಾಮನಪಾಯಿಪಯೋಭೃತಾಮ್।  
ರಜೋದುಷ್ಟೇಽಪಿ ಪಯಸಿ ಗ್ರಾಮಭೋಗೋ ನ ದುಷ್ಯತಿ॥

a325d3a1de.s:

a346adb3b7.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of Jyaiṣṭhaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
a346adb3b7.d:
The Abhidhyeyaka Abhishekam festival, also known as Jyeshthabhishekam, is a celebration held annually in the auspicious month of Jyeshtha, aligning with the Jyeshtha star in the constellation. The term “Abhidhyeyakam” refers to a protective shield or armour, symbolizing the divine defense that Bhagavan assumes in this Kaliyuga to combat evil. This festival, celebrated over three days, centers around a special abhishekam performed for this sacred armour.

According to temple traditions, this Abhishekam is conducted to safeguard the Utsava deities of Bhagavan Malayappa Swami and his consorts, Sridevi and Bhudevi. The purpose is to prevent any potential damage during various processions and holy baths (Tirumanjanam) throughout the year.

Each day of the festival, after the second bell, the deities are taken to the Kalyanotsava Mandapam situated in Sampangi Prakaram. Here, Snapana Tirumanjanam is performed, a ritual involving bathing the deities with consecrated water infused with spices, turmeric, sandal paste, honey, milk, and curd, accompanied by the chanting of Vedic mantras.

On each day, Bhagavan and his consorts are adorned in unique kavachams: The first day features the Vajrakavacham, a diamond-studded armour; the second day showcases the Muthyala kavacham, an armour studded with pearls; and the third day highlights the Svarna kavacham, a golden armour. The Svarna kavacham remains on the deities for the entire year and is only removed for the next Abhidhyeyaka Abhishekam.

a360e8fe45.s:
ಕಾಲಾದರ್ಶೇ—  
ಪೂರ್ವಶ್ಚೋರ್ಧ್ವಮನಧ್ಯಾಯಮಹಃ ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಮಣೇ ನಿಶಿ।  
ದಿವಾ ಪೂರ್ವೋತ್ತರಾ ರಾತ್ರಿರಿತಿ ವೇದವಿದೋ ವಿದುಃ॥

a383efb47d.d: Give arghyam to Agastya Maharshi during these three days.
a383efb47d.s:
ಕೃತ್ಯಸಾರಸಮುಚ್ಚಯಃ---  
ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವೈವರ್ತೇ---  
ಅಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇ ಭಾಸ್ಕರೇ ಕನ್ಯಾಂ ಶೇಷಭೂತೈತ್ರಿಭಿರ್ದಿನೈಃ।  
ಅರ್ಘಂ ದದ್ಯುರಗಸ್ತ್ಯಾಯ ಗೌಡದೇಶನಿವಾಸಿನಃ॥  
ನಾರಸಿಂಹೇ---  
ಶಙ್ಖೇ ತೋಯಂ ವಿನಿಕ್ಷಿಪ್ಯ ಸಿತಪುಷ್ಪಾಕ್ಷತೈರ್ಯುತಮ್।  
ಮನ್ತ್ರೇಣಾನೇನ ವೈ ದದ್ಯಾದ್ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಭಿಮುಖಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಃ॥  
ಅನೇನ ‘ಶಙ್ಖಂ ಪುಷ್ಪಂ ಫಲಂ ತೋಯಮ್’ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಮನ್ತ್ರೇಣ। ಅತ್ರ ದಿನತ್ರಯೇ ಮನ್ತ್ರತ್ರಯಂ ಯಥಾ---  
ಕುಮ್ಭಯೋನಿಸಮುತ್ಪನ್ನ ಮುನೀನಾಂ ಮುನಿಸತ್ತಮ।  
ಉದಯಂ ತೇ ಲಙ್ಕಾದ್ವಾರೇಽರ್ಘೋಽಯಂ ಪ್ರತಿಗೃಹ್ಯತಾಮ್॥೧॥  
ಶಙ್ಖಂ ಪುಷ್ಪಂ ಫಲಂ ತೋಯಂ ರತ್ನಾನಿ ವಿವಿಧಾನಿ ಚ।  
ಉದಯಂ ತೇ ಲಙ್ಕಾದ್ವಾರೇಽರ್ಘೋಽಯಂ ಪ್ರತಿಗೃಹ್ಯತಾಮ್॥೨॥  
ಕಾಶಪುಷ್ಪಪ್ರತೀಕಾಶ ವಹ್ನಿಮಾರುತಸಮ್ಭವ।  
ಉದಯಂ ತೇ ಲಙ್ಕಾದ್ವಾರೇಽರ್ಘೋಽಯಂ ಪ್ರತಿಗೃಹ್ಯತಾಮ್॥೩॥  
ಇತಿ ಕೇಚಿತ್। ರಸಮಾಲಾಯಾಂ ತು ಪ್ರಥಮದಿನೇ ತೃತೀಯಮನ್ತ್ರಃ, ದ್ವಿತೀಯೇ-ಪ್ರಥಮಮನ್ತ್ರಃ ಇತಿ ಭೇದಃ।

a38527907b.b: Observed on Śukla-Ēkādaśī tithi of Kārttikaḥ (lunar) month (Madhyāhnaḥ/puurvaviddha).
a38527907b.d: Bhishma, lying on śaratalpa performed upadesha to Yudhisthira and other Pandavas for these five days. On the eleventh day in the month of Kārttika, Bhisma requested for water, and his thirst was quenched by Arjun, who brought the water of Gaṅgā by an arrow. Hence, Lord Krishna blessed Bhisma that all the people should offer libations to Bhishma and propitiate him beginning from Ekadashi and ending on the full-moon day. The Skanda Purana describes this highly meritorious ritual, Bhīṣmapañcaka Vrata, performed over five days during the bright half of the month of Kārttika. It includes specific practices like offering libations and Arghya to Bhīṣma. This Vrata is noted for its difficulty; it includes the worship of Lord Hari, and the use of specific offerings like cowdung, honey, milk, and ghee for purification rituals. The observance of this Vrata brings immense spiritual benefits, including the eradication of sins and contentment for numerous births.
a38527907b.s:
ವಾಲಖಿಲ್ಯಾ ಊಚುಃ---  
ಕಾರ್ತಿಕಸ್ಯಾಽಮಲೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಸ್ನಾತ್ವಾ ಸಮ್ಯಗ್ಯತವ್ರತಃ।  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಂ ತು ಗೃಹ್ಣೀಯಾದ್ ವ್ರತಂ ಪಞ್ಚದಿನಾತ್ಮಕಮ್॥೧॥  
ಶರಪಞ್ಜರಸುಪ್ತೇನ ಭೀಷ್ಮೇಣ ತು ಮಹಾತ್ಮನಾ।  
ರಾಜಧರ್ಮಾ ಮೋಕ್ಷಧರ್ಮಾ ದಾನಧರ್ಮಾಸ್ತತಃ ಪರಮ್।  
ಕಥಿತಾ ಪಾಣ್ಡುದಾಯಾದೈಃ ಕೃಷ್ಣೇನಾಪಿ ಶ್ರುತಾಸ್ತದಾ॥೨॥  
ತತಃ ಪ್ರೀತೇನ ಮನಸಾ ವಾಸುದೇವೇನ ಭಾಷಿತಮ್।  
ಧನ್ಯಧನ್ಯೋಽಸಿ ಭೀಷ್ಮ ತ್ವಂ ಧರ್ಮಾಃ ಸಂಶ್ರಾವಿತಾಸ್ತ್ವಯಾ॥೩॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಂ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕಸ್ಯ ಯಾಚಿತಂ ಚ ಜಲಂ ತ್ವಯಾ।  
ಅರ್ಜುನೇನ ಸಮಾನೀತಂ ಗಾಙ್ಗಂ ಬಾಣಸ್ಯ ವೇಗತಃ॥೪॥  
ತುಷ್ಟಾನಿ ತವ ಗಾತ್ರಾಣಿ ತಸ್ಮಾದದ್ಯದಿನಾವಧಿ।  
ಪೂರ್ಣಾನ್ತಂ ಸರ್ವಲೋಕಾಸ್ತ್ವಾಂ ತರ್ಪಯನ್ತ್ವರ್ಘ್ಯದಾನತಃ॥೫॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಯತ್ನೇನ ಮಮ ಸನ್ತುಷ್ಟಿಕಾರಕಮ್।  
ಏತದ್ ವ್ರತಂ ಪ್ರಕುರ್ವನ್ತು ಭೀಷ್ಮಪಞ್ಚಕಸಂಜ್ಞಿತಮ್॥೬॥  
ಕಾರ್ತಿಕಸ್ಯ ವ್ರತಂ ಕೃತ್ವಾ ನ ಕುರ್ಯಾದ್ ಭೀಷ್ಮಪಞ್ಚಕಮ್।  
ಸಮಗ್ರಂ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕವ್ರತಂ ವೃಥಾ ತಸ್ಯ ಭವಿಷ್ಯತಿ॥೭॥  
ಅಶಕ್ತಶ್ಚೇನ್ನರೋ ಭೂಯಾದಸಮರ್ಥಶ್ಚ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ।  
ಭೀಷ್ಮಸ್ಯ ಪಞ್ಚಕಂ ಕೃತ್ವಾ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕಸ್ಯ ಫಲಂ ಲಭೇತ್॥೮॥  
ಸತ್ಯವ್ರತಾಯ ಶುಚಯೇ ಗಾಙ್ಗೇಯಾಯ ಮಹಾತ್ಮನೇ।  
ಭೀಷ್ಮಾಯೈತದ್ ದದಾಮ್ಯರ್ಘ್ಯಮಾಜನ್ಮಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚಾರಿಣೇ॥೯॥  
ಸವ್ಯೇನಾನೇನ ಮನ್ತ್ರೇಣ ತರ್ಪಣಂ ಸಾರ್ವವರ್ಣಿಕಮ್॥೧೦॥  
ವ್ರತಾಙ್ಗತ್ವಾತ್ ಪೂರ್ಣಿಮಾಯಾಂ ಪ್ರದೇಯಃ ಪಾಪಪೂರುಷಃ।  
ಅಪುತ್ರೇಣ ಪ್ರಕರ್ತವ್ಯಂ ಸರ್ವಥಾ ಭೀಷ್ಮಪಞ್ಚಕಮ್॥೧೧॥  
ಯಃ ಪುತ್ರಾರ್ಥಂ ವ್ರತಂ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ ಸಸ್ತ್ರೀಕೋ ಭೀಷ್ಮಪಞ್ಚಕಮ್।  
ಪ್ರದತ್ತ್ವಾ ಪಾಪಪುರುಷಂ ವರ್ಷಮಧ್ಯೇ ಸುತಂ ಲಭೇತ್॥೧೨॥  
ಅವಶ್ಯಮೇವ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಂ ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ ಭೀಷ್ಮಸ್ಯ ಪಞ್ಚಕಮ್।  
ವಿಷ್ಣುಪ್ರೀತಿಕರಂ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಂ ಮಯಾ ಭೀಷ್ಮಸ್ಯ ಪಞ್ಚಕಮ್॥೧೩॥  
ಇತಿ ಶ್ರೀಸ್ಕಾನ್ದೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣ ಏಕಾಶೀತಿಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಂ ದ್ವಿತೀಯೇ ವೈಷ್ಣವಖಣ್ಡೇ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕಮಾಸಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯೇ ಭೀಷ್ಮಪಞ್ಚಕವ್ರತಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯವರ್ಣನಂನಾಮ ದ್ವಾತ್ರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ॥೩೨॥

a4a49130a5.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and budhaḥ in maghā siṁhaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°37′23.82″.
a4a49130a5.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°37′23.82″, 0°37′06.27″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 0°54′43.25″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.70, elongation 8°32′36.71″ E). budhaḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 1°32′07.08″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.11, elongation 8°37′54.15″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

a760532a97.d:
The Wari (pilgrimage) is a centuries-old tradition in Maharashtra, India, involving a ceremonial procession of devotees (Warkaris) accompanying the Padukas (symbolic footprints) of saints to the Vithoba temple in Pandharpur. The two most prominent processions originate from the towns of Dehu and Alandi.

The pilgrimage of Sant Tukaram Maharaj (Sant Tukārāma Mahārāj) begins in the holy town of Dehu (dehū) on the banks of the Indrayani (indrāyaṇī) river. On the auspicious day of Jyeshtha Vadya Saptami (jyeṣṭha vadya saptamī), the silver pādukās are placed in the Pālkhī, and the procession departs from the Inamdar Wada. The first night is spent nearby in Ākurḍī before the Wārkarīs enter Pune, resting at the Nivdunga Vitthal Mandir in Nana Peth. As the journey moves into the rural heartland, the procession halts successively at Loṇī Kāl̤bhor), Yavat, and Varvaṇḍ. A major milestone is reached at Bārāmatī, where the Pālkhī rests for a day. The spiritual energy intensifies at Sansar, famous for its first Riṅgaṇ ceremony, followed by stops at Anthurṇe and Nimgaon Ketki. The route then winds through Indapur and halts at Sarāṭī on the riverbank. Entering the Solapur district, the procession witnesses a grand Ringan at Aklūj, followed by halts at Borgaon and Pirachi Kuroli. Finally, on Ashadhi Shuddha Dashami, the procession reaches the convergence point of Wākharī.

Those with janma nakshatra punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or anūrādhā (anujanma) or uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. a7d2414eeb.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and budhaḥ in rēvatī mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°38′09.00″.

Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) budhaḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

a88edf8ef3.d:
When Rohini nakshatra falls on a Saturday, it is a special yōgaḥ. In the cyclic rotation of time, along with the bad combinations of grahas and nakshatras that indicate the probability of upcoming difficulties, good combinations that grant benefits in multiples also arise. Among such good combinations are the Amrita Siddhi yogas of certain weekdays and nakshatras. They are Sunday-Hasta, Monday-Mrigashirsha, Tuesday-Ashvini, Wednesday-Anuradha, Thursday-Pushya, Friday-Revati, Saturday-Rohini. Good deeds performed on such yogas become especially strong in protecting and nourishing us.
For instance, in Devi Atharvashirsha, it is said bhaumāśvinyāṁ mahādevī-sannidhau japtvā mahāmr̥tyuṁ tarati, that is, one can cross even mahāmr̥tyu by doing parayanam when Tuesday and Ashvini join.

a9a4e41111.d:
कुम्भसंस्थे दिनकरे पौर्णम्यां पितृदैवते।
सकृत्सन्दर्शनात् शम्भो ब्रह्मघ्नकलुषं हर॥
---कुम्भघोण-माहात्म्ये ब्रह्म-प्रार्थना

कुम्भराशौ सूर्ये सति, खे विपरीतदिशि मघासु च चन्द्रमसि सति पर्वेदम्। 

एतादृशे दिने दाक्षायणी दक्षेण लब्धा। गुहेन शिवायोपदिष्टश्च प्रणवः। वराहेण पृथिवी चोद्धृता। 

कुम्भघोणक्षेत्रे स्नानस्य विशेषः। शिवानुग्रहेण तत्र सर्वा अपि नद्यः पापनिवृत्त्याय आयन्ति।

a9a59f0fd6.s:
ನಾರೀ ವಾ ವಿಧವಾ ವಾಽಪಿ ಪುತ್ರೀಪುತ್ರವಿವರ್ಜಿತಾ।  
ಸಭರ್ತೃಕಾ ಸಪುತ್ರಾ ವಾ ಕುರ್ಯಾದ್ ವ್ರತಮಿದಂ ಶುಭಮ್॥ (ಸ್ಕಾನ್ದೇ ಧರ್ಮವಚನಮ್)  
ಅವೈಧವ್ಯಂ ಚ ಸೌಭಾಗ್ಯಂ ದೇಹಿ ತ್ವಂ ಮಮ ಸುವ್ರತೇ।  
ಪುತ್ರಾನ್ ಪೌತ್ರಾಂಶ್ಚ ಸೌಖ್ಯಂ ಚ ಗೃಹಾಣಾರ್ಘ್ಯಂ ನಮೋಽಸ್ತು ತೇ॥  
ವಟ ಸಿಞ್ಚಾಮಿ ತೇ ಮೂಲಂ ಸಲಿಲೈರಮೃತೋಪಮೈಃ।  
ಯಥಾ ಶಾಖಾಪ್ರಶಾಖಾಭಿರ್ವೃದ್ಧೋಽಸಿ ತ್ವಂ ಮಹೀತಲೇ।  
ತಥಾ ಪುತ್ರೈಶ್ಚ ಪೌತ್ರೈಶ್ಚ ಸಮ್ಪನ್ನಂ ಕುರು ಮಾಂ ಸದಾ॥

aa00c47da1.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Prathamā tithi of every (lunar) month (Sāṅgavaḥ/paraviddha).
aa00c47da1.d: Anadhyayana on account of prathamā. Several tithis in a month are nitya-anadhyayana days, including prathamā, aṣṭamī, chaturdaśī, amāvāsyā and pūrṇimā. Manu has said that performing adhyayana on these days destroys the Guru (Amavasya), Shishya (Chaturdashi) and the vīrya of the brahma (vēda) itself (Ashtami/Purnima). Similarly, Jabali Rishi has said that Adhyayana on prathama hurts the buddhi while adhyayana on chaturdaśī hurts the brahma (vēda) itself! Interestingly, Bhagavan Hanuman also remarks while describing the condition of Sita Devi to the rest of the vanaras and Rkshas that she was frail by nature, had further grown emaciated, owing to separation from her beloved Shri Rama, much like the vidyā of a scholar continuing his studies on a pratipat!
aa00c47da1.s:
ಹಾರೀತಃ—  
ಪ್ರತಿಪತ್ಸು ಚತುರ್ದಶ್ಯಾಮಷ್ಟಮ್ಯಾಂ ಪರ್ವಣೋರ್ದ್ವಯೋಃ।  
ಶ್ವೋಽನಧ್ಯಾಯೇಽದ್ಯ ಶರ್ವರ್ಯಾಂ ನಾಧೀಯೀತ ಕದಾಚನ॥  
ಮನುಃ—  
ಅಮಾವಾಸ್ಯಾ ಗುರುಂ ಹನ್ತಿ ಶಿಷ್ಯಂ ಹನ್ತಿ ಚತುರ್ದಶೀ।  
ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾಷ್ಟಕಾಪೌರ್ಣಮಾಸ್ಯಸ್ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ತಾಃ ಪರಿವರ್ಜಯೇತ್॥  
ಜಾಬಾಲಿಃ—  
ನಾಧೀಯೀತ ನರೋ ನಿತ್ಯಮಾದಾವನ್ತೇ ಚ ಪಕ್ಷಯೋಃ।  
ಆದೌ ಚ ಹೀಯತೇ ಬುದ್ಧಿರನ್ತೇ ಚ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಹೀಯತೇ॥  
ಪಕ್ಷಾದಿಃ ಪ್ರತಿಪತ್, ಪಕ್ಷಾನ್ತಃ ಚತುರ್ದಶೀ॥  
ತಥಾ ರಾಮಾಯಣೇ ಹನುಮದ್ವಚನಮ್—

ಗತಂ ತದೈವ ಮೇ ಭಯಂ ತ್ವದಮ್ಬು ವೀಕ್ಷಿತಂ ಯದಾ

ತ್ವದೀಯಪಾದಪಙ್ಕಜಂ ನಮಾಮಿ ದೇವಿ ನರ್ಮದೇ॥

ತಾವನ್ತ್ಯೋ ಲಿಙ್ಗರೂಪಿಣ್ಯೋ ಭವಿಷ್ಯನ್ತಿ ವರಾನ್ಮಮ॥  
ದುಷ್ಪ್ರಾಪಂ ಯಜ್ಞತಪಸಾಂ ರಾಶಿಭಿಃ ಪರಮಾರ್ಥತಃ।

ab28bc5666.d:
The Krishna-paksha Ekadashi of chaitra month is known as varūthinī-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
ab28bc5666.s:
ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಚ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮುಪೋಷಣಮ್।  
ಯದೀಚ್ಛೇದ್ವಿಷ್ಣುಸಾಯುಜ್ಯಂ ಶ್ರಿಯಂ ಸನ್ತತಿಮಾತ್ಮನಃ।  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಂ ನ ಭುಞ್ಜೀತ ಪಕ್ಷಯೋರುಭಯೋರಪಿ॥  
  
ಅದ್ಯ ಸ್ಥಿತ್ವಾ ನಿರಾಹಾರಃ ಶ್ವೋಭೂತೇ ಪರಮೇಶ್ವರ।  
ಭೋಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಪುಣ್ಡರೀಕಾಕ್ಷ ಶರಣಂ ಮೇ ಭವಾಚ್ಯುತ॥  
ಪ್ರಮಾದಾದಥವಾಽಽಲಸ್ಯಾದ್ಧರೇ ಕೇಶವ ಮಾಧವ।  
ವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಸ್ಯ ಚ ವೈ ವಿಘ್ನೋ ನ ಭವೇತ್ತ್ವತ್ಪ್ರಸಾದತಃ॥  
--ಪದ್ಮಪುರಾಣೇ  
  
ಶ್ರೀಬ್ರಹ್ಮವೈವರ್ತೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಖಣ್ಡೇ ಸೌತಿಶೌನಕಸಂವಾದೇ ನಾರದಂ ಪ್ರತಿ ಶಿವೋಪದೇಶೇ ಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾದಿವಿವರಣಂ ನಾಮ ಸಪ್ತವಿಂಶತಿತಮೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ---  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮನಾಹಾರಂ ಗೃಹೀ ವಿಪ್ರಶ್ಚ ಭಾರತೇ।  
ಸ ಚ ತಿಷ್ಠತಿ ವೈಕುಣ್ಠೇ ಯಾವದ್ವೈ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣೋ ವಯಃ॥೧೪॥  
  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಫಲಂ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಂ ಪಾದ್ಮಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಶಙ್ಖೋದ್ಧಾರೇ ನರಃ ಸ್ನಾತ್ವಾ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ದೇವಂ ಗದಾಧರಮ್॥೩೫॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಷು ಚತುರ್ಲಕ್ಷಂ ಯೋ ದದಾತಿ ನೃಪೋತ್ತಮ॥೩೬॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಪ್ರಭಾಸಕ್ಷೇತ್ರೇ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಗ್ರಹಣೇ ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯಯೋಃ॥೩೭॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಕೇದಾರೇ ಚೋದಕಂ ಪೀತ್ವಾ ಪುನರ್ಜನ್ಮ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ॥೩೮॥  
ತಥಾ ಚೈಕಾದಶೀ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಗರ್ಭವಾಸಕ್ಷಯಙ್ಕರೀ।  
ಅಶ್ವಮೇಧಸ್ಯ ಯಜ್ಞಸ್ಯ ಪೃಥಿವ್ಯಾಂ ಯತ್ಫಲಂ ಲಭೇತ್॥೩೯॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತಪಸ್ವಿನೋ ಗೃಹೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಭುಞ್ಜತೇ ಚ ದ್ವಿಜೋತ್ತಮಾಃ॥೪೦॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಗೋಸಹಸ್ರೇಣ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ದತ್ವಾ ವೇದಾನ್ತಪಾರಗೇ॥೪೧॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಯೇಷಾಂ ದೇಹೇ ತ್ರಯೋ ದೇವಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿಷ್ಣುಮಹೇಶ್ವರಾಃ॥೪೨॥  
ವಸನ್ತಿ ತೇಷಾಂ ತೇ ತುಲ್ಯಾ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತೇ ನರಾಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಕರ್ಮಾಣೋ ಯೇ ಭಕ್ತಾ ಹರಿಪೂಜಕಾಃ॥೪೩॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಪುಣ್ಯಸಙ್ಖ್ಯಾ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ।  
ಏತತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಭವೇತ್ ತಸ್ಯ ಯತ್ಸುರೈರಪಿ ದುರ್ಲಭಮ್॥೪೪॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀಸಮಂ ನಾಸ್ತಿ ವ್ರತಂ ಪಾಪಪ್ರಣಾಶನಮ್॥೧೧೮॥  
---ಶ್ರೀಪಾದ್ಮೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಪಞ್ಚಪಞ್ಚಾಶತ್ಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಮುತ್ತರಖಣ್ಡೇ ಉಮಾಮಹೇಶ್ವರಸಂವಾದೇ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುತ್ಪತ್ತಿ-ಮುರವಧೋ ನಾಮ ಚತ್ವಾರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ॥೪೦॥

ab97a5a8a8.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Kaliya Nayanmar, a resident and oil merchant of Tiruvotriyur, was known for his deep devotion to Bhagavan Shiva, particularly expressed through his daily service of lighting lamps in the temple. Initially affluent, he faced a dramatic turn of fortune when Bhagavan, to demonstrate Kaliya Nayanmar's unwavering faith, led him into poverty. This sudden change in his circumstances also brought about a lack of support from his family.

In his commitment to continue his service to Bhagavan, Kaliya Nayanmar resorted to manual labour to earn enough to buy oil for the temple lamps. However, as his situation worsened, even this means became unfeasible. Driven to desperation, he considered selling his wife, but this plan too did not materialise, as no one was willing to buy her. Facing utter despair and determined to fulfill his service, Kaliya Nayanmar contemplated using his own blood as a substitute for the oil to keep the temple lamps burning! At this poignant moment of self-sacrifice, Bhagavan Shiva intervened, stopping Kaliya Nayanmar from harming himself, and blessed him, acknowledging his profound devotion and selfless service.
ab97a5a8a8.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

abccfc9019.d:
The temple of Sri Kalyana Venkateshwara Swamy, which has been a center of devotion from ancient times, once fell into disrepair. It was later renovated by Chinna Tirumalacharya, the grandson of Sri Tallapaka Annamacharya, as evidenced by an inscription dated March 22nd, 1510 CE at the temple's entrance. Despite regaining its glory for several years, the temple again faced neglect in the 20th century.

In 1940, an Archaka named Sri Sundara Raja Swamy from Kanchi, inspired by a dream in which Sri Kalyana Venkateshwara Swamy appeared, took it upon himself to clean the temple premises and resume regular pujas. He conveyed his dream to the villagers, narrating how Shri Venkateshwara Swamy manifested in the dream and instructed him to restore the temple's former splendor (Past Vaibhavam) by conducting Deepa Naivedya Aaradhana, after which Bhagavan vanished from the dream. On July 11, 1940, which was Ashada Shukla Paksha Shashti, Sundara Raja Swamy conducted a special puja, marking the day the deity revealed his divine form to devotees. This event led the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams to initiate the annual "Sakshatkara Vaibhavotsavams."

"Sakshatkaram" refers to the deity's holy appearance or Darshan. The Sakshatkara Vaibhavotsavam is a three-day festival that includes the day of the deity’s appearance (Ashada Shuddha Shasti) and the days immediately before and after. The first day of the celebration includes a procession of the deity, Sri Kalyana Venkateshwara Swamy, along with His consorts, on the Pedda Shesha Vahanam, from the temple to the Kalyana Mandapa, followed by Abhishekam and Unjal Seva in the evening. The second day features Hanumantha Vahana Seva, and the third day concludes with the Garuda Vahana Seva at night. These celebrations provide devotees the opportunity to witness the deity and receive blessings.

abcf776295.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śaniḥ in uttaraprōṣṭhapadā mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°27′36.78″.
abcf776295.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°27′36.78″, 0°27′26.06″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°36′42.09″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -0.17, elongation 22°36′41.91″ W). śaniḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°09′05.31″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.93, elongation 22°33′56.27″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

af966442ff.d:
The Shukla-paksha Ekadashi of chaitra month is known as kāmadā-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
af966442ff.s:
ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಚ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮುಪೋಷಣಮ್।  
ಯದೀಚ್ಛೇದ್ವಿಷ್ಣುಸಾಯುಜ್ಯಂ ಶ್ರಿಯಂ ಸನ್ತತಿಮಾತ್ಮನಃ।

ಶ್ರೀಬ್ರಹ್ಮವೈವರ್ತೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಖಣ್ಡೇ ಸೌತಿಶೌನಕಸಂವಾದೇ ನಾರದಂ ಪ್ರತಿ ಶಿವೋಪದೇಶೇ ಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾದಿವಿವರಣಂ ನಾಮ ಸಪ್ತವಿಂಶತಿತಮೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ---  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮನಾಹಾರಂ ಗೃಹೀ ವಿಪ್ರಶ್ಚ ಭಾರತೇ।  
ಸ ಚ ತಿಷ್ಠತಿ ವೈಕುಣ್ಠೇ ಯಾವದ್ವೈ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣೋ ವಯಃ॥೧೪॥  
  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಫಲಂ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಂ ಪಾದ್ಮಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಶಙ್ಖೋದ್ಧಾರೇ ನರಃ ಸ್ನಾತ್ವಾ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ದೇವಂ ಗದಾಧರಮ್॥೩೫॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಷು ಚತುರ್ಲಕ್ಷಂ ಯೋ ದದಾತಿ ನೃಪೋತ್ತಮ॥೩೬॥

ತಪಸ್ವಿನೋ ಗೃಹೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಭುಞ್ಜತೇ ಚ ದ್ವಿಜೋತ್ತಮಾಃ॥೪೦॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಗೋಸಹಸ್ರೇಣ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ದತ್ವಾ ವೇದಾನ್ತಪಾರಗೇ॥೪೧॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।

afb3a415ac.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and budhaḥ in uttarāṣāḍhā makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′01.00″.
afb3a415ac.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′01.00″, 0°40′56.15″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°06′35.67″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.17, elongation 16°01′11.79″ E). budhaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°47′36.67″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -0.85, elongation 16°04′48.63″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) budhaḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
